Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

pprof 2.0.0 (development)

A rewrite of pprof 1.0.3 that absorbs pprofR 0.2.0 and grplasso 1.0. The package is organised by analysis step, and every function takes a data frame with column names.

Data

  • pp_data() replaces fe_data_prep() and the data handling inside the 1.0.3 fitters: one prepared object (rows sorted by provider and patient in the C locale, patient rows kept in input order, provider sizes in patients or rows, cutoff with >=, flags for providers with no or all events).
  • pp_check() replaces data_check(): no caret or olsrr, thresholds as arguments, metrics returned.
  • sim_kecc() simulates data shaped like the KECC measures (patient-month binary or binomial days outcomes, patient random effect).

Logistic fixed-effect model (the pprofR engine under the unified interface)

  • fit_logistic_fe() replaces logis_fe(): binary or binomial outcomes, SerBIN or BAN.
  • test() replaces test_fe(): statistic (exact, score, Wald) x variance (naive, robust, stabilized) with one fixed set of output columns; the naive Wald statistic uses the case-mix variance (gamma_variance()), which does not depend on the covariate origin; the restricted score test of 1.0.3 is back as score_type = "restricted".
  • summary() replaces summary_fe_covar(); the likelihood-ratio refit respects the fit’s own bound.
  • confint() gives intervals for the provider effects; standardize() replaces SR_output() and maps those limits to the ratios and rates; direct_expectation() replaces direct_exp().
  • test_measure() replaces test_SM() and adds the log scale.

Linear, random-effect and correlated random-effect models (rewritten from 1.0.3)

  • pp_data() detects or takes an outcome type (binary, binomial, continuous); sim_kecc() simulates continuous outcomes.
  • fit_linear_fe() replaces linear_fe(): the within-provider regression instead of a dense block-diagonal centring matrix; gamma_variance() offers the case-mix variance (1.0.3’s “simplified”, exactly sigma^2 / n_i) and the “full” one; the provider and covariate tests use the t distribution with n - m - p degrees of freedom for every model-based statistic (1.0.3 mixed normal and t references); a patient-clustered robust variance is new.
  • fit_logistic_fe(penalty = "firth") replaces logis_firth() and extends it to binomial trials; the object is a logistic_fe fit, so every test and standardization applies. The kernel follows ParaFLR (UM-KevinHe/hpc-flr): per-provider work on independent threads, with the p x p reductions as whole-data matrix products so that the result does not depend on the thread count. test(statistic = "lr") adds ParaFLR’s likelihood-ratio test of one provider effect with the other parameters fixed (penalized likelihood for a Firth fit).
  • fit_logistic_re(), fit_logistic_cre(), fit_linear_re(), fit_linear_cre() replace logis_re(), logis_cre(), linear_re(), linear_cre() (lme4 wrappers): the random effects are coefficients$alpha, their conditional variances post_var; the CRE decomposition names its columns <x>_within and <x>_between and defaults to every covariate; the tests of the fixed effects use 2 * pnorm(-|z|) (1.0.3 computed 2 * (1 - pnorm(z)), wrong for negative statistics); standardization offers the observed (default) or the predicted numerator.
  • The direct standardized difference of the linear models is relative to the population (the row-weighted mean of the effects), as the direct ratio of the logistic models always was; 1.0.3 used the median for the linear model only.

Variable selection (rewritten from grplasso 1.0)

  • var_select() (lasso or group lasso) replace pp.lasso() and grp.lasso(): the same objective and coordinate-descent paths, now with binomial trials, a deterministic update order (grplasso permuted the coordinates at random inside the C++ code) and without the data race in its OpenMP loop; penalize and group name the covariates instead of positional vectors.
  • cv() replace cv.pp.lasso() and cv.grp.lasso(): folds are formed within each provider over patients (grplasso stratified rows on the outcome and could leave a provider out of a training set, which crashed its predict method), the deviance is averaged by fold with a fold-based standard error, and both lambda_min and lambda_1se are reported.
  • coef(), predict() and selected_covariates() work along the path; predict() takes a data frame and handles unseen providers explicitly (grplasso indexed the effects by position for numeric identifiers).
  • Discrete-time survival and stratified Cox selection move to the survival components.

Reference distributions and reliability (new; empirical null from the KECC production code and pprof_py)

  • Null models null_model() (theoretical, fixed or empirical): the empirical null is fitted with MASS::rlm within size groups. The default (grouping = "rank": the providers sorted by size dealt into blocks of ceiling(n / 4); estimator = "huber" with MASS defaults) is what the production PPPW and SFR code does; grouping = "quantile" with estimator = "bisquare", maxit = 1000, acc = 1e-8 is the production SMR code (and EmpiNull), "quantile" with the Huber default the production SHR code, and grouping = "cut" the Group_EN of the KECC measures paper. MM-estimation, tuning constants, a common mean, a fit mask and small-group handling are the options of pprof_py’s EmpiricalNull.
  • calibrate() refers a test() or test_measure() result to a null model (adjusted statistics, p-values, flags and inverted limits); every test() method and test_measure() take a null_model.
  • Inter-unit reliability translated from pprof_py: iur() with the direct, bootstrap and split-half methods, with iur_curve() and iur_stratified().

Still to come (in this order)

  • Cox O/E components, discrete-time survival and stratified Cox selection.
  • Plots.
  • var_select() (lasso or group lasso) on a survival outcome fit grplasso’s Strat.cox() (the Cox model stratified by provider, now with counting-process rows, case weights and offsets) and, with model = "discrete", pp.DiscSurv() (the discrete-time hazard model with period and provider effects, the provider effects identified by a zero median instead of a reference provider), both with a cyclic update order and without the hard-coded column names; cv() cross-validate them on the partial-likelihood deviance per event or the person-period deviance.

Interface

  • One entry point per analysis step, with S3 methods for every model class: test() (provider effects; was test_providers()), summary() (covariate coefficients; was test_covariates()), standardize(), confint(), calibrate(), coef(), vcov(), predict(); null_model(kind) for the theoretical, fixed and empirical nulls; iur(method) for the three reliability estimators; var_select(penalty) for the lasso and group-lasso paths with cv() on the path. test() and test_measure() also accept a null kind by name (null_model = "empirical").

Plots (ggplot2)

  • plot() methods, after pprof_py’s presentation layer and the 1.0.3 plots: a test() result gives a caterpillar plot, a funnel plot (limits from the same test, on the precision or the expected-count axis, one curve per empirical-null group when calibrated) or the flag shares by provider-size group; a standardize() result the observed-against-expected scatter or an observed-over-expected funnel; a summary() result a forest plot of the coefficients; an empirical null_model() the null-calibration panels; an iur() result the reliability curve; a var_select() path and its cv() the coefficient paths and the cross-validation curve. flag_stability() tabulates the flags of several tests (scenarios) and plots them.
